pairs.premise: The annual general meeting of the Kowloon Shipping Company was held on the third Thursday of October in the main hall of the Peninsula building. The chairman opened by noting that freight volumes across the Pacific routes had fallen eleven percent year on year, largely because two of the four Panamax vessels had been in dry dock for scheduled hull maintenance between March and July. The finance director then presented the audited accounts, which showed revenue of four hundred and twelve million dollars against operating costs of three hundred and eighty seven million, leaving an operating profit of twenty five million, down from forty one million the previous year. A shareholder from the floor asked whether the board intended to maintain the dividend at eighteen cents per share; the chairman replied that the board would recommend a reduced dividend of twelve cents, and that the difference would be retained to fund the acquisition of a fifth vessel, expected to be delivered in the second quarter of the following year. The resolution to approve the accounts was carried on a show of hands with no votes against.
pairs.label: neutral

pairs.premise: In the winter of that year the river froze solid for the first time in four decades. Children walked across it to the far bank where the mill stood empty, its windows long since broken by boys with stones. The mill had closed when the last owner died without issue and the estate passed to a cousin in the capital who had never seen it and never came. Snow lay on the wheel and the sluice gates were rusted open. Every few years someone from the council would propose that it be restored as a museum, and every few years the proposal would die for want of money. That winter a photographer from a national newspaper came and took a picture of the frozen river with the mill behind it, and the picture won a prize, and for a season the village had more visitors than it had had in thirty years, and then it did not.
